note.question: How can real-time sensor information reduce the cost of maintenance and unplanned downtime by a considerable amount?
note.overview: Unexpected failures of equipment can have severe consequences and costs. Such unexpected failures can be prevented by performing preventive replacement based on real-time degradation data. This paper studies a component that degrades according to a compound Poisson process and fails when the degradation exceeds the failure threshold.

components.formal: Algorithmic rule: This contrasts the prerequisite for stochastic ordering that these are aligned (Shaked and Shanthikumar 2007, theorem 1.A.3).
conditions: At each component age t ∈N0, for a given number of shock arrivals n ∈N0, there exists a control limit δ(n,t) ≤ξ, such that the optimal action is to carry out a preventive replacement if and only if x ≥δ(n,t).

The optimal control limit is nondecreasing in t because as the component ages without failing, the decision maker is increasingly assured that the current component degrades slowly relative to the general population of components.

conditions: Markov (deterministic) policy depending only on state (x, n, t) independent of the decision epoch τ ∈N0.
By proposition 1.2.2. of Bertsekas (2007), there exists an optimal Markov (deterministic) policy depending only on state (x, n, t) independent of the decision epoch τ ∈N0.

We are interested in finding the optimal replacement policy π∗ {πτ}τ∈N0 that minimizes the total expected discounted cost of corrective and preventive replacements over an infinite horizon, where the costs are discounted by a factor γ ∈(0,1).
This policy is a sequence of decision rules that prescribe whether to perform preventive maintenance if x < ξ.

sources.quote: Markov (deterministic) policy depending only on state (x, n, t) independent of the decision epoch τ ∈N0.
If the degradation level at a decision epoch does not exceed ξ, then we can either perform preventive replacement at cost cp or continue to the next decision epoch at no cost.
